task.title: Track and Finish an In-Progress Operation
task.shortdesc: See where a paused merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert stands, then abort, restart, or continue it.

context.p: When an operation pauses for conflicts, the Git Client shows where it stands. The view labels the operation in progress (for example, Merging), and the view marks the commits involved with amber labels. Your current commit is Start (Mine), and the incoming side is labeled by operation: Incoming (Theirs) for a merge, HEAD for a rebase, Cherry-picked commit, or Reverted commit. The node is joined by a dashed grey line to its parent commit, or to both parents when a merge is in progress.

fig.title: In-Progress Merge in the Git History View

step.cmd: Resolve any conflicts the operation reported.
Use the buttons in the conflict panel above the file list to finish or back out of the operation. The buttons depend on which operation is in progress:

ul.li: Abort - Restores the state from before the operation started.
Restart Merge - Reverts your working-copy changes so you can try a different strategy.
Continue Rebase - Completes the rebase once every conflict is resolved.

info.p: The panel stays visible after all conflicts are resolved (until you commit), so these actions remain available.
